Batch Seasonal Analysis, Smart-Linking, and Multi-Crop Modeling

Source: vignettes/batch-seasonal-analysis.Rmd
batch-seasonal-analysis.Rmd

Introduction

Agricultural water management rarely deals with a single isolated season. Water accounting studies, irrigation scheme audits, and yield forecasting projects typically require analyzing multiple consecutive years, rotational cropping seasons (e.g., Winter Wheat followed by Summer Maize), and spatially variable planting/harvesting dates across thousands of fields.

The Rwapor package provides a high-throughput Batch Seasonal Analysis Engine with Smart-Linking, allowing users to execute multi-year, multi-crop analyses seamlessly through both programmatic R scripts and the interactive Shiny Web GIS dashboard (run_wapor()).

1. Batch Architecture & Smart-Linking Mechanics

When running in batch mode, Rwapor executes an automated extraction loop over a list of named seasons. Rather than requiring users to manually crop, resample, and pass individual rasters for every season, the engine activates Smart-Linking:

Project Directory
├── seasonal_masks/
│   ├── Winter_2021_mask.tif    <── Automatically matched for "Winter_2021"
│   ├── Winter_2021_start.tif
│   ├── Winter_2021_end.tif
│   ├── Summer_2022_mask.tif    <── Automatically matched for "Summer_2022"
│   ├── Summer_2022_start.tif
│   └── Summer_2022_end.tif
└── ...

Supported Raster Naming Conventions

For each season label (e.g. Winter_2021), the engine automatically looks inside the project root directory and the seasonal_masks/ subfolder. Both suffix and prefix naming conventions are supported:

Layer Type Suffix Convention (Default) Prefix Convention (Alternative) Value Description
Crop Mask <Label>_mask.tif mask_<Label>.tif Integer crop class codes (1 = Wheat, 2 = Maize; 0 or NA = non-crop).
Season Start (SOS) <Label>_start.tif or <Label>_sos.tif start_<Label>.tif or sos_<Label>.tif Pixel-wise planting Day of Year (DOY 11–366366) or continuous Julian days.
Season End (EOS) <Label>_end.tif or <Label>_eos.tif end_<Label>.tif or eos_<Label>.tif Pixel-wise harvesting Day of Year (DOY 11–366366) or continuous Julian days.

[!NOTE] Cross-Year Seasons: In temperate and Mediterranean climates, winter crops are often planted in October/November (e.g. DOY 305) and harvested in April/May of the following calendar year (e.g. DOY 120). Rwapor automatically detects whenever EOS<SOS\text{EOS} < \text{SOS} pixel-wise and shifts the continuous Julian day reference by 365365 (or 366366 in leap years). You do not need to manually normalize cross-year dates.

2. Case 1: Pure Date-Driven Multi-Year Monitoring

For regional or basin-scale analyses where cropping calendars are relatively uniform or where satellite phenology rasters are not available, you can run batch mode with fixed date windows.

Step-by-Step Script 

library(Rwapor)

# 1. Define multi-season schedule as a named list of date pairs (YYYY-MM-DD)
seasons <- list(
  "Winter_2021" = c("2020-11-01", "2021-05-31"),
  "Winter_2022" = c("2021-11-01", "2022-05-31"),
  "Winter_2023" = c("2022-11-01", "2023-05-31")
)

# 2. Configure analysis settings
config <- list(
  period      = seasons,      # Pass the named list to activate batch mode
  aeti_var    = "L2-AETI-D",
  ret_var     = "L1-RET-D",
  precip_var  = "L1-PCP-D",
  npp_var     = "L2-NPP-D",
  t_var       = "L2-T-D",
  data_source = "local",
  folder      = "wapor_data", # Directory containing downloaded dekadal rasters
  indicators  = c("agg_aeti", "agg_ret", "etc", "adequacy_etc", "agg_pcp", "cwp_bwp")
)

# 3. Define crop parameters (applied to all AOI pixels in single-crop mode)
crop_wheat <- wapor_custom_crop(
  base_crop   = "Winter Wheat",
  class_value = 1L,
  kc_mid      = 1.15,
  HI          = 0.45
)

# 4. Execute batch run
batch_results <- wapor_run_seasonal_analysis(
  config      = config,
  crop_params = crop_wheat,
  rasters     = list() # No masks: entire area treated as class 1
)

# 5. Access results per season
names(batch_results)
# [1] "Winter_2021" "Winter_2022" "Winter_2023"

# Example: Inspect Winter 2022 AETI raster and summary metrics
w22_aeti <- batch_results$Winter_2022$seasonal_aeti$raster
w22_etc  <- batch_results$Winter_2022$seasonal_etc
print(batch_results$Winter_2022$cwp)

3. Case 2: Multi-Crop Batch Analysis with Auto-Linked Season Rasters

In complex irrigation schemes, different crops grow simultaneously across distinct parcels with different crop coefficients (KcK_c), stage lengths, and planting schedules.

File Organization

Place your season-specific rasters in your project folder’s seasonal_masks/ subfolder:

my_project/
  seasonal_masks/
    Season_2021_mask.tif     # Multi-class: 1 = Wheat, 2 = Sugarbeet, 3 = Alfalfa
    Season_2021_start.tif    # Pixel-wise SOS (DOY)
    Season_2021_end.tif      # Pixel-wise EOS (DOY)
    Season_2022_mask.tif
    Season_2022_start.tif
    Season_2022_end.tif

Multi-Crop Parameter Table Setup 

library(Rwapor)

# Define parameters for each crop class matching the mask integer values
wheat_params <- wapor_custom_crop(
  base_crop   = "Winter Wheat",
  class_value = 1L,
  crop_name   = "Durum Wheat",
  kc_mid      = 1.20,
  HI          = 0.48
)

sugarbeet_params <- wapor_custom_crop(
  base_crop   = "Sugarbeet",
  class_value = 2L,
  crop_name   = "Sugar Beet",
  kc_mid      = 1.20,
  HI          = 0.80
)

alfalfa_params <- wapor_custom_crop(
  base_crop   = "Alfalfa",
  class_value = 3L,
  crop_name   = "Alfalfa Hay",
  kc_mid      = 1.20,
  HI          = 0.90
)

# Combine into a single validated crop_params table
multi_crop_params <- wapor_combine_crop_params(
  wheat_params,
  sugarbeet_params,
  alfalfa_params
)

Running Batch Analysis with Auto-Linking 

config <- list(
  period      = list(
    "Season_2021" = c("2020-10-01", "2021-06-30"),
    "Season_2022" = c("2021-10-01", "2022-06-30")
  ),
  aeti_var    = "L2-AETI-D",
  ret_var     = "L1-RET-D",
  precip_var  = "L1-PCP-D",
  npp_var     = "L2-NPP-D",
  data_source = "local",
  folder      = "my_project",
  output_dir  = "my_project/analysis_outputs",
  indicators  = c("agg_aeti", "etc", "adequacy_etc", "agg_pcp", "cwp_bwp")
)

# The engine discovers Season_2021_* and Season_2022_* rasters in seasonal_masks/
results <- wapor_run_seasonal_analysis(
  config      = config,
  crop_params = multi_crop_params,
  rasters     = list() # Smart-linking automatically resolves rasters per season
)

# Export all outputs into structured per-season directories
wapor_export_analysis_outputs(
  results      = results,
  folder       = "my_project/analysis_outputs",
  indicators   = config$indicators,
  include_seasonal_tables = TRUE
)

Resulting Output Structure 

my_project/analysis_outputs/
├── Season_2021/
│   ├── seasonal_rasters/
│   │   ├── Season_2021_seasonal_aeti.tif
│   │   ├── Season_2021_seasonal_ret.tif
│   │   ├── Season_2021_seasonal_etc.tif
│   │   ├── Season_2021_adequacy_etc.tif
│   │   └── Season_2021_etc_class_1.tif
│   └── seasonal_tables/
│       └── Season_2021_summary_metrics.csv
└── Season_2022/
    ├── seasonal_rasters/
    └── seasonal_tables/

4. Case 3: Generating Season Rasters from Field Boundaries & Planting Tables

If you have vector boundaries of agricultural parcels and a spreadsheet of planting/harvesting dates from farmer surveys or farm management software, Rwapor can automatically build all the required GeoTIFF masks.

Required Input Format

  1. Vector File (parcels.geojson or parcels.shp): Contains polygon boundaries for each field, with an ID column (e.g. field_id).
  2. CSV Table (crop_calendar.csv): Contains recorded dates and crop types per field:
id season_name start_date end_date crop_type
P-101 Winter_2022 2021-11-05 2022-05-20 Wheat
P-102 Winter_2022 2021-11-12 2022-05-28 Wheat
P-103 Winter_2022 2021-10-25 2022-06-10 Sugarbeet
P-101 Summer_2022 2022-06-15 2022-09-30 Maize
P-102 Summer_2022 2022-06-20 2022-10-05 Maize

Generating Rasters Programmatically 

library(Rwapor)

# Load a template raster (e.g., an existing AETI or RET layer for grid alignment)
template_raster <- terra::rast("my_project/L2-AETI-D/WAPOR-3.L2-AETI-D.2022-01-01.tif")

# Generate all seasonal start, end, and crop mask rasters
mask_registry <- wapor_vector_to_season_rasters(
  vector_path   = "parcels.geojson",
  csv_path      = "crop_calendar.csv",
  template_r    = template_raster,
  vector_id_col = "field_id",
  csv_id_col    = "id",
  season_col    = "season_name",
  start_col     = "start_date",
  end_col       = "end_date",
  crop_col      = "crop_type",
  output_folder = "my_project/seasonal_masks"
)

print(mask_registry)
#        season                         start_raster                           end_raster                           crop_mask
# 1 Winter_2022 .../seasonal_masks/Winter_2022_start.tif .../seasonal_masks/Winter_2022_end.tif .../seasonal_masks/Winter_2022_mask.tif
# 2 Summer_2022 .../seasonal_masks/Summer_2022_start.tif .../seasonal_masks/Summer_2022_end.tif .../seasonal_masks/Summer_2022_mask.tif

Once generated, these files are immediately recognized by wapor_run_seasonal_analysis() in batch mode!

5. Case 4: Interactive Batch Analysis in the Shiny Dashboard

You can execute the entire batch workflow without writing a line of code using the Rwapor Shiny Dashboard.

  1. Launch the App:

    Rwapor::run_wapor()

  2. Navigate to the Analysis Tab:

    • In the sidebar, select your project folder.

  3. Step 1: Enable Batch Mode:

    • Check the Batch Mode checkbox.

    • Click the [?] Batch Guide link at any time to review syntax and file conventions.

    • Enter your seasons in the text area (one per line, format: Label, Start, End):

      Winter_2021, 2020-11-01, 2021-05-31
Summer_2022, 2022-06-01, 2022-09-30
Winter_2022, 2021-11-01, 2022-05-31

    • Tip: If you already downloaded seasonal data in the Download tab, click Detect to auto-scan your folder and fill the table automatically, or Copy DL to import the periods defined during download.

  4. Step 2: Masking & Timing:

    • If you have field boundary polygons and a date CSV, check Generate from Vector & CSV, upload your files, map your columns, and click Update Masks.

  5. Step 3: Crop Specs:

    • Review and customize FAO-56 crop parameters (KcK_c, Stage lengths, Harvest Index) for each detected class.

  6. Step 4: Indicator Selection:

    • Use the grouped checklist or click [Core] or [All] to select your target indicators.

  7. Run & Review:

    • Click Run Analysis. The progress bar tracks execution across all seasons.
    • View results in the Seasonal Indicators unified table and switch to the Visualisation tab to explore spatial rasters.
